change: definition: "Bhagavad Gītā 1–3: The self in which the one of steady wisdom is content 'by the self' (2.55) and in which one who has nothing to do delights and is satisfied (3.17); that which is beyond the understanding, by which the self is steadied (3.42–43, saḥ). Also used reflexively and for the person or mind (vidheyātmā 2.64; vimūḍhātmā 3.6, 3.27; ātmavān 2.45). The embodied self of 2.12–30 is called dehin or śarīrin." -> "Bhagavad Gītā 1–3: The self in which the one of steady wisdom is content — in the self alone, by the self (2.55) — and in which one who has nothing to do delights and is satisfied (3.17); knowing what is beyond the understanding (which 3.42 calls only 'he', saḥ; the commentators take it as the self), one steadies the self by the self (ātmānam ātmanā, 3.43). Also used reflexively and for one's person, nature or mind (vidheyātmā 2.64; vimūḍhātmā 3.6, 3.27; ātmavān 2.45; kāmātmānaḥ 2.43). The embodied one of 2.12–30 is called dehin or śarīrin, not ātman."
reason: The old definition identified 3.42's 'he' (saḥ) with the ātman as if the text said so; that is the commentators' reading. Also aligned with the corrected 2.55 ('in the self alone').
